crop.notes: Whole 'A Robber's Remorse' article, headline to end, across two column pieces. Allen is mentioned once, in crop 6.

ocr.notes: Mostly right; scattered errors (e.g. 'St. Ronis Duly', 'Ilansen', '$3S' for $65). The Allen passage is read correctly.

title.suggested: Reformed Robber Blames Gamblers Who Made the Allen-Goss Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reprinted a New York Times story in which a pardoned bank robber said his ruin began in a Cincinnati gambling house kept by the men who made the Allen-Goss fight, Hochheimer & Co. and Eph Holland.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat--Supplemental Sheet, page 12; the date is not visible in the page image but fits the reprint from the New York Times of March 19 [1877].

facts.fact: A former convict said the Allen-Goss fight had been made by the Cincinnati gamblers Hochheimer & Co. and Eph Holland, who kept a gambling saloon on Fifth Street

notes: Allen is only mentioned in passing, inside the robber's account. The article does not say which Allen-Goss fight he meant.
